title: Binary Trees: Structure, Traversal, and Use Cases
description: This module dives into binary trees, one of the most fundamental and powerful data structures in computer science. Learners will understand how binary trees are structured, the different types (full, complete, perfect, balanced, etc.), and how to implement them in JavaScript. The module focuses heavily on traversal algorithms—both recursive and iterative approaches—including preorder, inorder, postorder, and level order traversals. Advanced lessons introduce applications like expression trees, BST (Binary Search Tree) validation, height and depth calculations, and the relationship between recursion and tree processing. Real-world use cases help cement why binary trees are important, and learners will build problem-solving intuition with practical challenges.

lessons.title: What is a Binary Tree? Types and Properties
lessons.content:
A Binary Tree is a tree data structure where each node has at most two children: `left` and `right`.

**Types of Binary Trees**:
- Full Binary Tree: All nodes have 0 or 2 children.
- Complete Binary Tree: All levels are filled except possibly the last, which is filled from left to right.
- Perfect Binary Tree: All internal nodes have 2 children, and all leaves are at the same level.
- Balanced Binary Tree: The height difference between left and right subtrees of any node is at most 1.

Used in: Expression trees, heaps, and binary search trees.

Binary Tree Use Cases in Real Life and Coding
lessons.content:
**Common Applications**:
- **Expression Trees**: Represent arithmetic expressions.
- **File System Hierarchies**: Recursive folder structure.
- **Game Trees**: AI decision trees in chess, tic-tac-toe.
- **Compiler Syntax Trees**: Used in parsing expressions.
- **Balanced BSTs (like AVL or Red-Black Trees)** for database indexing.

Binary trees are foundational to many more complex structures like heaps, tries, and segment trees.
